blocks.title: <ico-book></ico-book> THE THREAD
blocks.intro: A listener cannot go back and reread. To keep them with you, you need two things: signposts that say where the next sentence is going, and pointing words that link back without repeating. That is cohesion.

vocab.sp: concession: what comes next limits what I just said

vocab.en: what's more / on top of that
vocab.sp: addition: one more point in the same direction
return: back to the main line

vocab.en: to cut a long story short

vocab.sp: reference: the first / the second of two
reference: of the kind just mentioned

blocks.note: How it works: two versions of the same monologue , compare , gap-fill , rewrite , order and memory. Press CHECK wherever you see it.

parts.html: 1 · SIGNPOSTS AND POINTING BACK — the two halves of cohesion

items.en: The show ran long. That said, nobody left.
items.sp: A signpost: «That said» warns you that a contrast is coming.

items.en: We tried two formats. The latter worked.
items.sp: Pointing back: «the latter» = the second format. No repetition.

parts.html: 2 · CONCESSION — yes, but. They open the second sentence and take a comma

items.en: The studio is small. That said, it sounds great.
items.sp: That said, = I accept the first point; here is the other side.

items.en: It was expensive. Even so, we bought it.
items.sp: Even so, = in spite of that (a surprising result).

items.en: He's always late. Mind you, he's never missed a show.
items.sp: Mind you, = spoken; an afterthought that softens what you said.

items.en: It was a disaster. Having said that, I'd do it again.
items.sp: Having said that, = a little more formal than «that said».

parts.html: 3 · SPOKEN MARKERS — add a point, come back, jump to the end

items.en: The app is fast. What's more, it's free.
I missed the bus. On top of that, it started to rain.
Anyway, as I was saying, the car broke down.
items.sp: Return: you wandered off, and now you come back.

items.en: To cut a long story short, we missed the show.

parts.html: 4 · POINT BACK WITHOUT REPEATING — the former, the latter, do so, such, one

items.en: We could cut the news or the weather. The former is longer; the latter is more popular.
items.sp: the former = the news · the latter = the weather. Only with two things.

items.en: Listeners asked us to change the time, and we did so.

items.sp: such = of the kind I just mentioned.

items.en: I liked the first script more than the second one.

parts.body: Read it aloud. If every sentence opens with a marker, half of them are noise. A marker earns its place only when the direction changes: a contrast, an extra point, a return, the end. Two or three in a minute of speech is plenty.

parts.html: SPANISH TRAP — conectores que se parecen y no son iguales

items.en: On the other hand, the price is fair.
items.sp: «Por otro lado» = on the other hand. Nunca by ni in.

items.en: Lastly, I'd like to thank the team.
Even though it rained, we went.
It rained. Even so, we went.
items.sp: «Aun así» = even so, y empieza frase nueva.

parts.body: By the other hand,… → On the other hand,… · Even it rained, we went. → Even though it rained, we went. · Y recuerda: actually = en realidad, no «actualmente».

blocks.title: <ico-star></ico-star> THE THREAD
blocks.intro:
Every week, Theo, the co-host, records a monologue. This week's runs seven minutes, and it wanders. Roz hands you the transcript: «Make it three, and make it flow.»

WORDS OF THE DAY (they must appear in your writing): to ramble = to talk for too long without a clear line · to cut a long story short · to lose the thread.

blocks.title: AUDIO 1 · THE RAMBLE
blocks.desc: Theo's first take, before any editing. The story is good. Listen to how he joins his ideas, and to where he loses the thread.

questions.q: Why did Theo start cycling to work?
options: His brother gave him a bicycle

questions.q: What did he notice on the third day?
Why is this version hard to follow?
options: He uses too many rare words
Nearly every idea is joined with "and" or "so", and he wanders off the story

questions.q: Which phrase shows that he has lost the thread?
options: Three weeks is a long time.

speaking.prompt: Rescue one part of the ramble. Say the 'car broke down' section again in three sentences, with one marker.
speaking.starter: In March, the car broke down, and… A neighbor lent me… Even so,…

transcript.html: So, this week I want to talk about bicycles. And I never liked bicycles. And I never liked cyclists, really, because they go through red lights, and they ride on the sidewalk, and so I always took the car. And the car is comfortable, and the car is warm, and I've had my car for eleven years. Eleven years! My brother sold me that car. He lives by the coast now, my brother, and he's got a boat, which is, well, that's another story. Where was I? The car.

So the car broke down in March. And the garage said three weeks. And three weeks is a long time. And so my neighbor lent me a bicycle, an old green bicycle, and I didn't want the bicycle, but I took the bicycle. And the first day was terrible, and it rained, and I arrived late, and I arrived wet. And the second day was terrible.

And so on the third day something happened, and I noticed the river. And I've lived in this city for twenty years, and I never noticed the river on my way to work. And I noticed a bakery, and I noticed that I wasn't angry when I arrived. And in the car I'm always angry when I arrive.

And so the garage called, and the car was ready, and I got the car back, and the car was fine. And so I drove the car for a week. And I was angry for a week. And so I bought a bicycle. And I still don't like cyclists who go through red lights. And so that's what I wanted to say about bicycles.

blocks.title: UNLINKED vs LINKED
blocks.intro: The same three facts about the rooftop studio. In one version the listener has to do the work; in the other, the speaker does it.

pair.a: The studio is small. It is cold. We love it.
pair.b: The studio is small and cold. Even so, we love it.

items.q: Which version is easier to follow?
What does "Even so" tell the listener?
options: The opposite of what you'd expect is coming

items.q: Which marker could replace "Even so" in B?
Add one more good thing about the studio. Which sentence works?
options: Even so, the view is amazing.
What's more, the view is amazing.
The former, the view is amazing.
Even though it was late, we stayed.
Even so it was late, we stayed.
Even it was late, we stayed.

blocks.title: CHOOSE THE MARKER
blocks.intro: Read both sentences first. Which way does the second one go: contrast, addition, return, summary, or pointing back?

items.q: The tickets were expensive. ___, we bought them.
The guest was funny. ___, she was on time.
options: To cut a long story short

items.q: Sorry, I got distracted. ___, as I was saying, the car broke down.
We missed the bus, the train was late and the taxi got lost. ___, we arrived at midnight.
options: To cut a long story short

items.q: We tested a morning show and a night show. ___ had more listeners.
They asked us to shorten the program, and we ___.
He never reads the script. ___, his show is the most popular.
options: To cut a long story short

items.q: ___ it was raining, we recorded outside.
First the news, then the weather and, ___, the interview.
The rent is high. ___, the location is perfect.

blocks.title: AUDIO 2 · THE EDIT
blocks.desc: The same story after the edit: half the length, and you never get lost. Compare it with Audio 1: what was cut, and which markers do the work?

questions.q: In Audio 1, Theo said "I didn't want the bicycle, but I took the bicycle." Which marker does the job now?
What was cut from the first version?
"I went back to the former for one week, and then I bought the latter." What is "the latter"?
Which marker introduces the one opinion Theo has not changed?
options: To cut a long story short

speaking.prompt: Tell me in 30 seconds about something you changed your mind about. Use one concession marker and finish with 'To cut a long story short,…'.
speaking.starter: For years, I… Then… Even so,… To cut a long story short,…

transcript.html: This week: something I changed my mind about. Bicycles. For years I couldn't stand them, or the people who rode them. Cyclists went through red lights and rode on the sidewalk, so I stayed in my car.

Then, in March, the car broke down, and the garage needed three weeks. A neighbor lent me an old green bicycle. I didn't want it. Even so, I took it. The first two days were miserable: I arrived late and wet. On the third day, though, I noticed the river. I've lived in this city for twenty years, and I had never once seen it on my way to work. What's more, I arrived calm. In the car, I never do.

When the garage called, I had a choice: the car or a bicycle. I went back to the former for one week, and then I bought the latter. Mind you, I still can't stand cyclists who go through red lights. Anyway, to cut a long story short: I was wrong about bicycles. Just not about all cyclists.

blocks.title: JOIN THEM
blocks.intro: Link the two ideas with the marker in gold. The first sentence is already in the box when it stays the same.

items.source: It was expensive. We bought it.
answers: It was expensive. Even so, we bought it.

items.source: The studio is small. It sounds great.
answers: The studio is small. That said, it sounds great.

items.source: The guest was late. She forgot her notes.
answers: The guest was late. What's more, she forgot her notes.
The guest was late. What's more, she had forgotten her notes.
items.why: What's more, + a second point in the same direction.

items.source: It was raining. We recorded outside.
answers: Even though it was raining, we recorded outside.
We recorded outside even though it was raining.
items.why: even though + clause, in the same sentence.

items.source: We could cut the news or the weather. The weather is more popular.
items.start: We could cut the news or the weather.
answers: We could cut the news or the weather. The latter is more popular.
items.why: the latter = the second of the two.

items.source: They asked us to change the time. We changed the time.
items.start: They asked us to change the time, and
answers: They asked us to change the time, and we did so.

blocks.title: BUILD THE PARAGRAPH
blocks.intro: Each chip is one sentence. The markers and pointing words tell you the order.

words: I used to hate mornings.
Then I got a dog.
Now I'm up at six every day.
What's more, I enjoy it.
items.answer: I used to hate mornings. Then I got a dog. Now I'm up at six every day. What's more, I enjoy it.

words: The studio is on the roof.
In winter, it is freezing up there.
Even so, nobody wants to move.
After all, the view is too good to lose.
items.answer: The studio is on the roof. In winter, it is freezing up there. Even so, nobody wants to move. After all, the view is too good to lose.

words: We had two guests last night, a chef and a pilot.
The former talked about bread.
The latter talked about storms.
Both were excellent.
items.answer: We had two guests last night, a chef and a pilot. The former talked about bread. The latter talked about storms. Both were excellent.

words: My train was canceled.
On top of that, it started to rain.
Anyway, I got here in the end.
So, what did I miss?
items.answer: My train was canceled. On top of that, it started to rain. Anyway, I got here in the end. So, what did I miss?

words: Radio is cheap to make.
That said, it is hard to make well.
For one thing, you need a good script.
Without one, even a great host will ramble.
items.answer: Radio is cheap to make. That said, it is hard to make well. For one thing, you need a good script. Without one, even a great host will ramble.

blocks.title: MEMORY · the marker and its job
blocks.intro: Find each marker and what it does. Tap two cards.

pairs.a: to cut a long story short

blocks.title: <ico-pen></ico-pen> THE THREE-MINUTE SCRIPT
blocks.intro: Write a short monologue for the show (about 120 words): something I changed my mind about. It will be read aloud, so the listener must never get lost.
checklist: One concession marker (that said / even so / mind you / having said that)
One addition marker (what's more / on top of that)
One return or summary marker (anyway / as I was saying / to cut a long story short)
One pointing word (the former / the latter / do so / such / one)
The words of the day, and no more than four markers in total: pass the overuse test
blocks.example: For years, I old opinion. Then what happened. concession marker, the surprise. What's more, a second reason. I had two choices: A or B. I chose the former / latter. To cut a long story short, new opinion.
blocks.hw: Write your script, then record it without rambling: under one minute, one take. Send me the text and the audio on WhatsApp.

rubric.d: About 120 words, with a clear before and after: what you thought, what happened, what you think now.
One marker of each kind and one pointing word, each used with the right meaning and punctuation, and not one more than you need.
A listener follows it in one hearing. No word-for-word translation from Spanish.
